title: Sampling degradation detector and runtime guardrails for tracing hotpath
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Recent changes to tracing sampling heuristics and a kernel upgrade caused an unexpected increase in per-request CPU and tail P99 latency in high-QPS services. Root cause is occasional sampling config regressions and lack of automatic mitigation when hotpath latency or allocation pressure increases.

Goal: Implement a lightweight runtime detector that continuously evaluates whether tracing sampling configuration is degrading service hotpath performance, and wire simple guardrails to reduce tracing hotpath overhead automatically (without losing all observability). Provide dashboards, alerts, and a canary rollout path.

Scope / Acceptance criteria:
- A detector running in the request proxy (or inference gateway) that emits a single low-cardinality metric: sampling_degradation_score (0-100) computed from: emitted_span_rate_per_1k_requests, hotpath_alloc_bytes, request_handler_p99_latency, and sampling_config_change_epochs.
- A guardrail policy engine that triggers one of three mitigation modes when score exceeds thresholds: 1) prefiler-only (drop trace payloads, keep counters), 2) probabilistic-minimal (sample ~0.1%), 3) full-disable (only critical traces retained). The engine must be configurable per-route and per-tenant.
- Mitigations must switch within 200ms of breach and record a decision_audit event for debugging.
- New dashboards: sampling-regression-detector (per-route score, mitigation state, before/after P50/P99) and a cross-service heatmap to help triage root causes.
- Playbook + alert: trigger when score>70 for 2m in two distinct nodes.
- Rollout behind feature flag with canary to 5% of traffic, automatic rollback if customer-impacting errors increase >0.5%.

Design notes / trade-offs:
- We intentionally keep the detector logic simple (moving window aggregates + EWMA) to avoid adding CPU/alloc pressure. More complex ML-based detectors were considered but rejected for the initial rollout.
- We avoid storing per-trace state; detector uses low-cardinality counters to keep memory usage small.
- Audit events are batched asynchronously to minimize hotpath cost. Initial audit sampling set to 1% to allow debugging while controlling overhead.

Progress updates:
- 2026-03-10: Spike completed to measure current baseline on two canary services; found median sampling overhead 3.1% CPU, P99 +18ms on heavy QPS. (Aisha)
- 2026-03-11: Design doc drafted and shared: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OBS/Sampling+Degradation+Detector (internal). High-level design approved by Observability leads. (Diego)
- 2026-03-12: Prototype detector implemented in proxy sidecar (Go) and landed an internal test harness. Unit tests for EWMA and scoring rules added. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/proxy/pull/842 (WIP). (Diego)
- 2026-03-13: Guardrail policy engine POC added; mitigation switching works locally. Began instrumenting metrics for: sampling_degradation_score, mitigation_mode, detector_decision_count, audit_event_emitted. Connected metrics to staging Prometheus. (Diego)
- 2026-03-14: Canary config created; dashboards skeleton pushed to Grafana: dashboards/grafana/sampling-detector-overview. Security reviewed audit event schema; no PII included. Planning canary rollout to 5% traffic next week. (Aisha)
notes:
Review feedback from infra: ensure detector uses read-only metrics where possible to avoid locking. Prod SRE requested a per-tenant opt-out. We added opt-out label support.

Open questions:
- Exact numeric thresholds for score->mitigation mapping (proposal: 40->prefilter, 60->prob-minimal, 80->full-disable). Need perf tests to validate.
- How long to persist mitigation state after score returns <threshold? (initial plan: decay window 30s).
blockers: Need an infra credential to deploy sidecar image to canary cluster; security team requested a short review of audit event schema (in progress).
next_steps:
